faq.q: Is "Lower Landing" a real Richmond place name?
faq.a: No City of Richmond source read uses "Lower Landing." The official name for this Steveston waterfront pocket is London Landing — it is in the City's Zoning Bylaw as the "London Landing (Steveston)" zones and on the ground at London's Wharf Park, 6062 Dyke Road; this page is written on that basis, pending Jared's confirmation.

faq.q: Where does the London Landing name come from?
faq.a: Steveston heritage material records that in 1881 brothers Charles and William London bought 200 acres at the south end of No. 2 Road at what became known as London's Landing.

faq.q: What homes are in London Landing?
faq.a: Strata-led waterfront product: mixed-use buildings under the site-specific ZMU20/ZMU24 London Landing (Steveston) zones (The Pier at London Landing, 6160 London Road; Harbour Walk, 13040 No. 2 Road), townhouses at 13200 Princess Street, and detached houses in RS1/RS2 at the edges.

faq.q: What is being built on No. 2 Road in London Landing?
faq.a: As of the July 8, 2026 staff report, Jim Pattison Developments' application RZ 25-009451 proposes rezoning 12771–13131 No. 2 Road from Light Industrial to a new ZMU63 London Landing (Steveston) zone for a five- and six-storey residential and commercial mixed-use project — an application in process, not an approval.

faq.q: What waterfront recreation is at London Landing?
faq.a: London's Wharf Park at 6062 Dyke Road — just under 4 acres with the No. 2 Road Pier, river views, a playground and open lawn — plus the South Dyke Trail and Steveston Greenways connections, and the historic London's Landing fishing pier area with its float, picnic tables and interpretation signage.
